interpretations: Signed Z extrema [a,b] yield max Q=max(a^2,b^2); if a<=0<=b then hull-derived lower Q=0 is conservative but need not be attainable. Exact lower Q needs the closest attainable Z to zero.

KM/risk constraints couple records, allow variable within-arm event/censor histories, and may exclude endpoint/switch extremizers. An outer relaxation can ignore constraints safely only if every compatible true-tied history is represented and the bounding result applies.
Preserving true ties requires weak orders and the tied hypergeometric variance; replacing ties by arbitrary strict orders is not justified by the inspected no-tie theorems.
Restricting queries to arm/time exact risk counts is an application-specific test family. A one-step minimax split is a heuristic, not a proof of globally minimum query cost.
No search miss or unavailable article is used as proof of priority.
